Step 2 of 2 BUILT: the Adjust tool. New MpiToolOptionsMaskAdjust in the Mask group (second button, after Brush) - one bidirectional Shrink/Grow slider, an Edge button that swaps that ONE row for Outward + Inward, live preview in the pending green, explicit Apply + Reset, MpiMaskStrip with brush false. ONE primitive read three ways: MaskManager._morph(src,r) blurs by |r| then thresholds alpha, low side dilates and high side erodes off the SAME blur, and an edge band is dilate(out) minus erode(in). ONE pristine snapshot, not two layers: the preview contract guarantees no picks survive into this tool, so maskCanvas at entry already IS manual minus subtract - beginAdjust copies that single canvas and every frame recomputes from it, so anti-compounding falls out of the design and UndoStack.pendingLayer() was not needed (that function now has NO consumer and docs/masking-undo.md says so). Apply is a layer-wide one shot: _recordUndo() after the no-op guard, manual gets the preview, subtract is CLEARED because the preview already has the erases baked in, then it publishes through onMaskStrokeEnd so shrink-to-empty relocks the op strip. el.discardPreview() gained the Adjust branch - the first tool to extend the seam instead of the call site, exactly as the contract predicted for 368/373. MEASURED not assumed (Chromium, 1536x1536, drawn 300px circle): r of 1,2,3,5,8,12 move the edge EXACTLY r px both directions; r=20 gives 19/21 and r=50 gives 47/54, which is curvature on a 300px circle rather than the threshold, so the textbook levels ARE the calibrated ones and the slider stays in real pixels with no fudge table. 8.7 ms per pass, 17.2 ms for a band - live at the working size, so the SVG feComponentTransfer was never needed and the apply-on-release fallback never triggered.
